verses.en: And when it was determined that we should sail into Italy, they delivered Paul and certain other prisoners unto one named Julius, a centurion of Augustus’ band.
verses.pt: E, como se determinou que navegássemos para a Itália, entregaram Paulo e alguns outros presos a um centurião por nome Júlio, da coorte augusta.
verses.en_web: When it was determined that we should sail for Italy, they delivered Paul and certain other prisoners to a centurion named Julius, of the Augustan band.
verses.en_bbe: And when the decision had been made that we were to go by sea to Italy, they gave Paul and certain other prisoners into the care of a captain named Julius, of the Augustan band.

verses.en: And entering into a ship of Adramyttium, we launched, meaning to sail by the coasts of Asia; one Aristarchus, a Macedonian of Thessalonica, being with us.
verses.pt: E, embarcando em um navio de Adramítio, que estava prestes a navegar em demanda dos portos pela costa da Ásia, fizemo-nos ao mar, estando conosco Aristarco, macedônio de Tessalônica.
verses.en_web: Embarking in a ship of Adramyttium, which was about to sail to places on the coast of Asia, we put to sea; Aristarchus, a Macedonian of Thessalonica, being with us.
verses.en_bbe: And we went to sea in a ship of Adramyttium which was sailing to the sea towns of Asia, Aristarchus, a Macedonian of Thessalonica, being with us.

verses.en: And the next day we touched at Sidon. And Julius courteously entreated Paul, and gave him liberty to go unto his friends to refresh himself.
verses.pt: No dia seguinte chegamos a Sidom, e Júlio, tratando Paulo com bondade, permitiu-lhe ir ver os amigos e receber deles os cuidados necessários.
verses.en_web: The next day, we touched at Sidon. Julius treated Paul kindly, and gave him permission to go to his friends and refresh himself.
verses.en_bbe: And on the day after, we came to Sidon; and Julius was kind to Paul, and let him go to see his friends and take a rest.

verses.en: And when we had launched from thence, we sailed under Cyprus, because the winds were contrary.
verses.pt: Partindo dali, fomos navegando a sotavento de Chipre, porque os ventos eram contrários.
verses.en_web: Putting to sea from there, we sailed under the lee of Cyprus, because the winds were contrary.
verses.en_bbe: And sailing again from there, we went on under cover of Cyprus, because the wind was against us.

verses.en: And when we had sailed over the sea of Cilicia and Pamphylia, we came to Myra, a city of Lycia.
verses.pt: Tendo atravessado o mar ao longo da Cilícia e Panfília, chegamos a Mirra, na Lícia.
verses.en_web: When we had sailed across the sea which is off Cilicia and Pamphylia, we came to Myra, a city of Lycia.
verses.en_bbe: And having gone across the sea off Cilicia and Pamphylia we came to Myra, in Lycia.

verses.en: And there the centurion found a ship of Alexandria sailing into Italy; and he put us therein.
verses.pt: Ali o centurião achou um navio de Alexandria que navegava para a Itália, e nos fez embarcar nele.
verses.en_web: There the centurion found a ship of Alexandria sailing for Italy, and he put us on board.
verses.en_bbe: And there the captain came across a ship of Alexandria, sailing for Italy, and put us in it.

verses.en: And when we had sailed slowly many days, and scarce were come over against Cnidus, the wind not suffering us, we sailed under Crete, over against Salmone;
verses.pt: Navegando vagarosamente por muitos dias, e havendo chegado com dificuldade defronte de Cnido, não nos permitindo o vento ir mais adiante, navegamos a sotavento de Creta, à altura de Salmone;
verses.en_web: When we had sailed slowly many days, and had come with difficulty opposite Cnidus, the wind not allowing us further, we sailed under the lee of Crete, opposite Salmone.
verses.en_bbe: And when we had gone on slowly for a long time, and had had hard work getting across to Cnidus, for the wind was against us, we went under cover of Crete, in the direction of Salmone;

verses.en: And, hardly passing it, came unto a place which is called The fair havens; nigh whereunto was the city of Lasea.
verses.pt: e, costeando-a com dificuldade, chegamos a um lugar chamado Bons Portos, perto do qual estava a cidade de Laséia.
verses.en_web: With difficulty sailing along it we came to a certain place called Fair Havens, near the city of Lasea.
verses.en_bbe: And sailing down the side of it, as well as we were able, we came to a certain place named Fair Havens, near which was the town of Lasea.

verses.en: Now when much time was spent, and when sailing was now dangerous, because the fast was now already past, Paul admonished them,
verses.pt: Havendo decorrido muito tempo e tendo-se tornado perigosa a navegação, porque já havia passado o jejum, Paulo os advertia,
verses.en_web: When much time had passed and the voyage was now dangerous, because the Fast had now already gone by, Paul admonished them,
verses.en_bbe: And as a long time had gone by, and the journey was now full of danger, because it was late in the year, Paul put the position before them,

verses.en: And said unto them, Sirs, I perceive that this voyage will be with hurt and much damage, not only of the lading and ship, but also of our lives.
verses.pt: dizendo-lhes: Senhores, vejo que a viagem vai ser com avaria e muita perda não só para a carga e o navio, mas também para as nossas vidas.
verses.en_web: and said to them, “Sirs, I perceive that the voyage will be with injury and much loss, not only of the cargo and the ship, but also of our lives.”
verses.en_bbe: Saying, Friends, I see that this journey will be one of great damage and loss, not only to the goods and the ship, but to ourselves.

verses.en: Nevertheless the centurion believed the master and the owner of the ship, more than those things which were spoken by Paul.
verses.pt: Mas o centurião dava mais crédito ao piloto e ao dono do navio do que às coisas que Paulo dizia.
verses.en_web: But the centurion gave more heed to the master and to the owner of the ship than to those things which were spoken by Paul.
verses.en_bbe: But the captain gave more attention to the master and the owner of the ship than to what Paul said.

verses.en: And because the haven was not commodious to winter in, the more part advised to depart thence also, if by any means they might attain to Phenice, and there to winter; which is an haven of Crete, and lieth toward the south west and north west.
verses.pt: E não sendo o porto muito próprio para invernar, os mais deles foram de parecer que daí se fizessem ao mar para ver se de algum modo podiam chegar a Fênice, um porto de Creta que olha para o nordeste e para o sueste, para ali invernar.
verses.en_web: Because the haven was not suitable to winter in, the majority advised going to sea from there, if by any means they could reach Phoenix, and winter there, which is a port of Crete, looking northeast and southeast.
verses.en_bbe: And as the harbour was not a good one in which to be for the winter, the greater number of them were for going out to sea, in order, if possible, to put in for the winter at Phoenix, a harbour of Crete, looking to the north-east and south-east.

verses.en: And when the south wind blew softly, supposing that they had obtained their purpose, loosing thence, they sailed close by Crete.
verses.pt: Soprando brandamente o vento sul, e supondo eles terem alcançado o que desejavam, levantaram ferro e iam costeando Creta bem de perto.
verses.en_web: When the south wind blew softly, supposing that they had obtained their purpose, they weighed anchor and sailed along Crete, close to shore.
verses.en_bbe: And when the south wind came softly, being of the opinion that their purpose might be effected, they let the ship go and went sailing down the side of Crete, very near to the land.

verses.en: But not long after there arose against it a tempestuous wind, called Euroclydon.
verses.pt: Mas não muito depois desencadeou-se do lado da ilha um tufão de vento chamado euro-aquilão;
verses.en_web: But before long, a stormy wind beat down from shore, which is called Euroclydon.
verses.en_bbe: But after a little time, a very violent wind, named Euraquilo, came down from it with great force.

verses.en: And when the ship was caught, and could not bear up into the wind, we let her drive.
verses.pt: e, sendo arrebatado o navio e não podendo navegar contra o vento, cedemos à sua força e nos deixávamos levar.
verses.en_web: When the ship was caught, and couldn’t face the wind, we gave way to it, and were driven along.
verses.en_bbe: And when the ship got into the grip of it, and was not able to make headway into the wind, we gave way, and went before it.

verses.en: And running under a certain island which is called Clauda, we had much work to come by the boat:
verses.pt: Correndo a sota-vento de uma pequena ilha chamada Clauda, somente a custo pudemos segurar o batel,
verses.en_web: Running under the lee of a small island called Clauda, we were able, with difficulty, to secure the boat.
verses.en_bbe: And, sailing near the side of a small island named Cauda, we were able, though it was hard work, to make the ship's boat safe:

verses.en: Which when they had taken up, they used helps, undergirding the ship; and, fearing lest they should fall into the quicksands, strake sail, and so were driven.
verses.pt: o qual recolheram, usando então os meios disponíveis para cingir o navio; e, temendo que fossem lançados na Sirte, arriaram os aparelhos e se deixavam levar.
verses.en_web: After they had hoisted it up, they used cables to help reinforce the ship. Fearing that they would run aground on the Syrtis sand bars, they lowered the sea anchor, and so were driven along.
verses.en_bbe: And having got it up, they put cords under and round the ship; but fearing that they might be pushed on to the Syrtis, they let down the sails and so went running before the wind.

verses.en: And we being exceedingly tossed with a tempest, the next day they lightened the ship;
verses.pt: Como fôssemos violentamente açoitados pela tempestade, no dia seguinte começaram a alijar a carga ao mar.
verses.en_web: As we labored exceedingly with the storm, the next day they began to throw things overboard.
verses.en_bbe: And, still fighting the storm with all our strength, the day after they made a start at getting the goods out of the ship;

verses.en: And the third day we cast out with our own hands the tackling of the ship.
verses.pt: E ao terceiro dia, com as próprias mãos lançaram os aparelhos do navio.
verses.en_web: On the third day, they threw out the ship’s tackle with their own hands.
verses.en_bbe: And on the third day, they let all the sailing apparatus go over the side.

verses.en: And when neither sun nor stars in many days appeared, and no small tempest lay on us, all hope that we should be saved was then taken away.
verses.pt: Não aparecendo por muitos dia nem sol nem estrelas, e sendo nós ainda batidos por grande tempestade, fugiu-nos afinal toda a esperança de sermos salvos.
verses.en_web: When neither sun nor stars shone on us for many days, and no small storm pressed on us, all hope that we would be saved was now taken away.
verses.en_bbe: And as we had not seen the sun or stars for a long time, and a great storm was on us, all hope of salvation was gone.

verses.en: But after long abstinence Paul stood forth in the midst of them, and said, Sirs, ye should have hearkened unto me, and not have loosed from Crete, and to have gained this harm and loss.
verses.pt: Havendo eles estado muito tempo sem comer, Paulo, pondo-se em pé no meio deles, disse: Senhores, devíeis ter-me ouvido e não ter partido de Creta, para evitar esta avaria e perda.
verses.en_web: When they had been long without food, Paul stood up in the middle of them, and said, “Sirs, you should have listened to me, and not have set sail from Crete, and have gotten this injury and loss.
verses.en_bbe: And when they had been without food for a long time, Paul got up among them and said, Friends, it would have been better if you had given attention to me and not gone sailing out from Crete, to undergo this damage and loss.

verses.en: And now I exhort you to be of good cheer: for there shall be no loss of any man’s life among you, but of the ship.
verses.pt: E agora vos exorto a que tenhais bom ânimo, pois não se perderá vida alguma entre vós, mas somente o navio.
verses.en_web: Now I exhort you to cheer up, for there will be no loss of life among you, but only of the ship.
verses.en_bbe: But now, I say to you, be of good heart, for there will be no loss of life, but only of the ship.

verses.en: For there stood by me this night the angel of God, whose I am, and whom I serve,
verses.pt: Porque esta noite me apareceu um anjo do Deus de quem eu sou e a quem sirvo,
verses.en_web: For there stood by me this night an angel, belonging to the God whose I am and whom I serve,
verses.en_bbe: For this night there came to my side an angel of the God who is my Master and whose servant I am,

verses.en: Saying, Fear not, Paul; thou must be brought before Caesar: and, lo, God hath given thee all them that sail with thee.
verses.pt: dizendo: Não temas, Paulo, importa que compareças perante César, e eis que Deus te deu todos os que navegam contigo.
verses.en_web: saying, ‘Don’t be afraid, Paul. You must stand before Caesar. Behold, God has granted you all those who sail with you.’
verses.en_bbe: Saying, Have no fear, Paul, for you will come before Caesar, and God has given to you all those who are sailing with you.

verses.en: Wherefore, sirs, be of good cheer: for I believe God, that it shall be even as it was told me.
verses.pt: Portanto, senhores, tende bom ânimo; pois creio em Deus que há de suceder assim como me foi dito.
verses.en_web: Therefore, sirs, cheer up! For I believe God, that it will be just as it has been spoken to me.
verses.en_bbe: And so, O men, be of good heart, for I have faith in God that it will be as he said to me.

verses.en: Howbeit we must be cast upon a certain island.
verses.pt: Contudo é necessário irmos dar em alguma ilha.
verses.en_web: But we must run aground on a certain island.”
verses.en_bbe: But we will be sent on to a certain island.

verses.en: But when the fourteenth night was come, as we were driven up and down in Adria, about midnight the shipmen deemed that they drew near to some country;
verses.pt: Quando chegou a décima quarta noite, sendo nós ainda impelidos pela tempestade no mar de Ádria, pela meia-noite, suspeitaram os marinheiros a proximidade de terra;
verses.en_web: But when the fourteenth night had come, as we were driven back and forth in the Adriatic Sea, about midnight the sailors surmised that they were drawing near to some land.
verses.en_bbe: But when the fourteenth day came, while we were going here and there in the Adriatic sea, about the middle of the night the sailors had an idea that they were getting near land;

verses.en: And sounded, and found it twenty fathoms: and when they had gone a little further, they sounded again, and found it fifteen fathoms.
verses.pt: e lançando a sonda, acharam vinte braças; passando um pouco mais adiante, e tornando a lançar a sonda, acharam quinze braças.
verses.en_web: They took soundings, and found twenty fathoms. After a little while, they took soundings again, and found fifteen fathoms.
verses.en_bbe: And they let down the lead, and saw that the sea was a hundred and twenty feet deep; and after a little time they did it again and it was ninety feet.

verses.en: Then fearing lest we should have fallen upon rocks, they cast four anchors out of the stern, and wished for the day.
verses.pt: Ora, temendo irmos dar em rochedos, lançaram da popa quatro âncoras, e esperaram ansiosos que amanhecesse.
verses.en_web: Fearing that we would run aground on rocky ground, they let go four anchors from the stern, and wished for daylight.
verses.en_bbe: Then, fearing that by chance we might come on to the rocks, they let down four hooks from the back of the ship, and made prayers for the coming of day.

verses.en: And as the shipmen were about to flee out of the ship, when they had let down the boat into the sea, under colour as though they would have cast anchors out of the foreship,
verses.pt: Procurando, entrementes, os marinheiros fugir do navio, e tendo arriado o batel ao mar sob pretexto de irem lançar âncoras pela proa,
verses.en_web: As the sailors were trying to flee out of the ship, and had lowered the boat into the sea, pretending that they would lay out anchors from the bow,
verses.en_bbe: Then the sailors made attempts secretly to get away from the ship, letting down a boat as if they were about to put down hooks from the front of the ship;

verses.en: Paul said to the centurion and to the soldiers, Except these abide in the ship, ye cannot be saved.
verses.pt: disse Paulo ao centurião e aos soldados: Se estes não ficarem no navio, não podereis salvar-vos.
verses.en_web: Paul said to the centurion and to the soldiers, “Unless these stay in the ship, you can’t be saved.”
verses.en_bbe: But Paul said to the captain and his men, If you do not keep these men in the ship, you will not be safe.

verses.en: Then the soldiers cut off the ropes of the boat, and let her fall off.
verses.pt: Então os soldados cortaram os cabos do batel e o deixaram cair.
verses.en_web: Then the soldiers cut away the ropes of the boat, and let it fall off.
verses.en_bbe: Then the armed men, cutting the cords of the boat, let her go.

verses.en: And while the day was coming on, Paul besought them all to take meat, saying, This day is the fourteenth day that ye have tarried and continued fasting, having taken nothing.
verses.pt: Enquanto amanhecia, Paulo rogava a todos que comessem alguma coisa, dizendo: É já hoje o décimo quarto dia que esperais e permaneceis em jejum, não havendo provado coisa alguma.
verses.en_web: While the day was coming on, Paul begged them all to take some food, saying, “Today is the fourteenth day that you wait and continue fasting, having taken nothing.
verses.en_bbe: And when dawn was near, Paul gave them all orders to take food, saying, This is the fourteenth day you have been waiting and taking no food.

verses.en: Wherefore I pray you to take some meat: for this is for your health: for there shall not an hair fall from the head of any of you.
verses.pt: Rogo-vos, portanto, que comais alguma coisa, porque disso depende a vossa segurança; porque nem um cabelo cairá da cabeça de qualquer de vós.
verses.en_web: Therefore I beg you to take some food, for this is for your safety; for not a hair will perish from any of your heads.”
verses.en_bbe: So I make request to you to take food; for this is for your salvation: not a hair from the head of any of you will come to destruction.

verses.en: And when he had thus spoken, he took bread, and gave thanks to God in presence of them all: and when he had broken it, he began to eat.
verses.pt: E, havendo dito isto, tomou o pão, deu graças a Deus na presença de todos e, partindo-o começou a comer.
verses.en_web: When he had said this, and had taken bread, he gave thanks to God in the presence of all, and he broke it, and began to eat.
verses.en_bbe: And when he had said this and had taken bread, he gave praise to God before them all, and took a meal of the broken bread.

verses.en: Then were they all of good cheer, and they also took some meat.
verses.pt: Então todos cobraram ânimo e se puseram também a comer.
verses.en_web: Then they all cheered up, and they also took food.
verses.en_bbe: Then they all took heart and did the same.

verses.en: And we were in all in the ship two hundred threescore and sixteen souls.
verses.pt: Éramos ao todo no navio duzentas e setenta e seis almas.
verses.en_web: In all, we were two hundred seventy-six souls on the ship.
verses.en_bbe: And we were, in the ship, two hundred and seventy-six persons.

verses.en: And when they had eaten enough, they lightened the ship, and cast out the wheat into the sea.
verses.pt: Depois de saciados com a comida, começaram a aliviar o navio, alijando o trigo no mar.
verses.en_web: When they had eaten enough, they lightened the ship, throwing out the wheat into the sea.
verses.en_bbe: And when they had had enough food, they made the weight of the ship less, turning the grain out into the sea.

verses.en: And when it was day, they knew not the land: but they discovered a certain creek with a shore, into the which they were minded, if it were possible, to thrust in the ship.
verses.pt: Quando amanheceu, não reconheciam a terra; divisavam, porém, uma enseada com uma praia, e consultavam se poderiam nela encalhar o navio.
verses.en_web: When it was day, they didn’t recognize the land, but they noticed a certain bay with a beach, and they decided to try to drive the ship onto it.
verses.en_bbe: And when it was day, they had no knowledge of the land, but they saw an inlet of the sea with a floor of sand, and they had the idea of driving the ship up on to it if possible.

verses.en: And when they had taken up the anchors, they committed themselves unto the sea, and loosed the rudder bands, and hoised up the mainsail to the wind, and made toward shore.
verses.pt: Soltando as âncoras, deixaram-nas no mar, largando ao mesmo tempo as amarras do leme; e, içando ao vento a vela da proa, dirigiram-se para a praia.
verses.en_web: Casting off the anchors, they left them in the sea, at the same time untying the rudder ropes. Hoisting up the foresail to the wind, they made for the beach.
verses.en_bbe: So cutting away the hooks, and letting them go into the sea, and freeing the cords of the guiding-blades, and lifting up the sail to the wind, they went in the direction of the inlet.

verses.en: And falling into a place where two seas met, they ran the ship aground; and the forepart stuck fast, and remained unmoveable, but the hinder part was broken with the violence of the waves.
verses.pt: Dando, porém, num lugar onde duas correntes se encontravam, encalharam o navio; e a proa, encravando-se, ficou imóvel, mas a popa se desfazia com a força das ondas.
verses.en_web: But coming to a place where two seas met, they ran the vessel aground. The bow struck and remained immovable, but the stern began to break up by the violence of the waves.
verses.en_bbe: And coming to a point between two seas, they got the ship to land; and the front part was fixed in the sand and not able to be moved, but the back part was broken by the force of the waves.

verses.en: And the soldiers’ counsel was to kill the prisoners, lest any of them should swim out, and escape.
verses.pt: Então o parecer dos soldados era que matassem os presos para que nenhum deles fugisse, escapando a nado.
verses.en_web: The soldiers’ counsel was to kill the prisoners, so that none of them would swim out and escape.
verses.en_bbe: Then the armed men were for putting the prisoners to death, so that no one would get away by swimming.

verses.en: But the centurion, willing to save Paul, kept them from their purpose; and commanded that they which could swim should cast themselves first into the sea, and get to land:
verses.pt: Mas o centurião, querendo salvar a Paulo, estorvou-lhes este intento; e mandou que os que pudessem nadar fossem os primeiros a lançar-se ao mar e alcançar a terra;
verses.en_web: But the centurion, desiring to save Paul, stopped them from their purpose, and commanded that those who could swim should throw themselves overboard first to go toward the land;
verses.en_bbe: But the captain, desiring to keep Paul safe, kept them from their purpose, and gave orders that those who had knowledge of swimming were to go off the ship and get first to land:

verses.en: And the rest, some on boards, and some on broken pieces of the ship. And so it came to pass, that they escaped all safe to land.
verses.pt: e que os demais se salvassem, uns em tábuas e outros em quaisquer destroços do navio. Assim chegaram todos à terra salvos.
verses.en_web: and the rest should follow, some on planks, and some on other things from the ship. So they all escaped safely to the land.
verses.en_bbe: And the rest, some on boards and some on things from the ship. And so it came about that they all got safe to land.
